name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behavior on social media, the researcher's signature methodological contribution (CooRnet, CLSB) now extended into automated alerting and encyclopedic/handbook treatments of coordination and manipulation.

name: Platform Data Access & Governance
description: Research on the shifting infrastructure of platform-mediated research access — CrowdTangle's shutdown, Meta's URL Shares Dataset, API politics in the Digital Services Act era, and platform content-moderation policies (e.g. Meta's political content reduction) — and their consequences for studying social media.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Disinformation
description: Emerging work on how generative AI reshapes information operations and persuasion tactics — synthetic visual persuasion in coordinated gambling promotion, LLM-driven deceptive campaigns, and the broader long-term effects of AI-generated content on public discourse — paired with a new graduate course on generative AI and media.

name: Italian Electoral Communication
description: The core MINE research line mapping Italian news media, political parallelism, and social media dynamics across the 2018, 2019 and 2022 Italian elections, including partisan attention, hyperpartisan networks, and parliamentarians' Facebook visibility.

name: Computational Text Methods & LLMs
description: Methodological work on applying and validating large language models and embedding techniques for content classification, annotation, and clustering of political news and social media text, including cross-team validation of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines for communication research.

name: Health Misinformation in Global Contexts
description: Studies of coordinated networks circulating problematic health information — including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration and Gates Foundation–funded work mapping health misinformation networks in India and Nigeria — alongside earlier work on Italian health information gatekeeping.

name: Polarization & Partisan Media Dynamics
description: Analysis of political polarization, partisan alignment, and algorithmic amplification in social and traditional media, spanning affective engagement in partisan communities, insularity/cross-partisan interaction patterns, and conceptual reviews of polarization and populism.

name: Cross-National Disinformation Monitoring
description: Comparative international projects tracking coordinated behavior and political information campaigns beyond Italy — the 2021 German federal election, Brazilian post-Bolsonaro digital battlegrounds, and Latin American platform polarization studies — often conducted with international collaborators via vera.ai and PROMPT.

name: Information Disorder & Fake News Theory
description: Foundational theoretical and taxonomic work on misinformation within the hybrid media system, including the widely cited fake news taxonomy and continued conceptual essays on manipulation and digital influence.

name: Social Media Audience Engagement
description: Long-running research strand on how audiences engage with media content via social platforms — from social TV/second-screen participation to Facebook reactions and citizen engagement in institutional campaigns — tracing continuity between early social-TV studies and current engagement metrics research.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.
